verification.notes: The declassified CIA Inspector General document identifies Project MOCKINGBIRD as a March–June 1963 telephone-intercept activity targeting two Washington journalists. It does not describe taking over television networks or coordinating their broadcasts, directly contradicting the asserted project description.

sources.title: CIA Inspector General report — Project MOCKINGBIRD
sources.relevance: Official declassified record defines the project as a limited telephone-intercept activity rather than takeover of television networks.

verification.notes: Senate records confirm historical CIA relationships with journalists and concern that covert media operations could manipulate public opinion. However, documented CIA-media relationships and Project MOCKINGBIRD predated the November 1963 JFK assassination, and the claim that the alliance began afterward to control minds overstates and misdates the record.
